name: US-Japan Trade Agreement (USJTA)
claim: Lighthizer and Ambassador Sugiyama signed the Trade Agreement and the Digital Trade Agreement on 7 Oct 2019; the goods agreement covers tariffs on some goods but not autos (per CRS IN12152). Entry-into-force date and any current USTR status page not confirmed.

name: US-Japan Digital Trade Agreement
claim: CRS (Apr 2026) describes the DTA as an executive agreement enacted without changes to US law; no source found showing termination or amendment, and I could not confirm the 1 Jan 2020 entry-into-force date.

name: US-Japan Critical Minerals Agreement (CMA)
claim: Signed 28 Mar 2023 and in force on signature without congressional approval; covers cobalt/graphite/lithium/manganese/nickel; no export duties; consult on non-market measures and forced-labour imports; Treasury/USTR treated it as an FTA for the IRA EV credit critical-minerals test.

name: Section 30D clean vehicle credit terminated (reduces CMA's IRA function)
claim: IRS says the new clean vehicle credit (30D) is not allowed for vehicles acquired after 30 Sep 2025, so the CMA's IRA-credit eligibility function is largely moot; no source found on any formal CMA amendment or termination (status in force but unreviewed).

name: US-Japan Agreement joint statement (July 2025 deal)
claim: Japan government text states that for any Section 232 tariff on pharmaceuticals and semiconductors (incl. SME) the US intends to apply to Japan a rate no greater than that applied to any other country; search snippet only, full document not read.

name: Executive Order 14345 Implementing the US-Japan Agreement
claim: EO signed 4 Sep 2025 sets 15% all-in tariff on Japanese goods (reciprocal) and a Section 232 auto/auto-parts rate that tops MFN up to 15% (added rate zero at or above 15%); the IEEPA part was later invalidated (see E08). Read via search summaries only.

name: US-Japan MOU on Strategic Investment (Japan-US Strategic Investment Initiative)
source: CSIS analysis (MOU text at cas.go.jp not machine-readable)
claim: MOU signed 4 Sep 2025 (Lutnick/Akazawa): presidential investment committee chaired by Commerce Secretary consults a joint consultation committee; US proposes projects; Japan has 45 days to fund each approved project or may decline and forfeit distributions (President may raise tariffs); per-project SPVs split cash 50/50 then 90/10 to the US after a deemed allocation amount; investments before 19 Jan 2029; US Investment Accelerator executes.

name: Supreme Court strikes down IEEPA tariffs; Section 122 surcharge
claim: On 20 Feb 2026 the Court ruled 6-3 that IEEPA does not authorise tariffs, removing the legal basis of the 15% Japan reciprocal rate; a temporary Section 122 global surcharge replaced it; Section 232 duties (autos etc.) unaffected.

name: Section 301 forced-labour tariffs replace Section 122 (12.5% on Japan)
claim: Jiji reports the US imposed new 12.5% Section 301 tariffs on Japan and dozens of partners after the Section 122 surcharge expired 24 Jul 2026; Japan called it regrettable and the 15% auto rate is said to be maintained; a separate excess-capacity 301 probe (launched Mar 2026) includes Japan. Check USTR Federal Register notice for final rate.

name: Section 232 tariffs on semiconductors (Jan 2026 proclamation) and Japan treatment
claim: A Jan 2026 proclamation imposed a 25% Section 232 duty on certain semiconductors; whether Japan's no-worse-than-others commitment (E05) caps it is not confirmed; exact date unverified.

name: Section 232 steel/aluminium/copper tariffs on Japan
claim: Only a low-quality tracker lists 50% on steel/aluminium/copper for Japan; no official source or Japan-specific exemption found, so current rate unverified.

name: US-Japan Framework for Securing the Supply of Critical Minerals and Rare Earths through Mining and Processing
claim: Framework text dated 27 Oct 2025 (signed Tokyo 28 Oct) commits to financing within six months for selected projects (grants/guarantees/loans/equity/offtake/insurance), a ministerial within 180 days, faster permitting, pricing measures to support non-China supply, scrap recycling, a complementary stockpile arrangement, and a Rapid Response Group led by the US Energy Secretary and METI Minister; names no dollar amounts and is non-binding.

name: US-Japan Critical Minerals Supply Security Rapid Response Group
claim: Framework establishes a group led by the US Energy Secretary and Japan's METI Minister to identify priority minerals and accelerate processed-mineral deliveries; whether it has met is unverified.

name: US-Japan Action Plan on Critical Minerals
claim: Greer announced the Action Plan on 19 Mar 2026: the two countries will develop strategic trade policies and border mechanisms to protect downstream industries and lay the foundation for a binding plurilateral agreement supported by price floors; trade press adds deep-sea R&D (not read from primary).

name: SII first batch: industrial synthetic diamond manufacturing
claim: Commerce lists industrial synthetic diamond manufacturing at about $0.6bn in the first batch announced 17 Feb 2026; the Georgia site and Element Six (De Beers) operator come from secondary reporting only.

name: SII first batch: US crude oil export infrastructure (reported as Texas GulfLink)
claim: Commerce lists US crude oil export infrastructure at about $2.1bn in the first batch (17 Feb 2026); Sentinel Midstream's Texas GulfLink identification comes from secondary reporting only.

name: SII first batch: natural gas generation (reported as 9.2 GW Ohio)
claim: Commerce lists natural gas generation at about $33.3bn (first batch total about $36bn); the Ohio location and 9.2 GW size come from the Lutnick statement as quoted in secondary coverage.

name: SII second batch: GE Vernova Hitachi SMRs (Tennessee and Alabama)
claim: Second batch announced 19 Mar 2026 at the Takaichi-Trump summit lists SMRs by GE Vernova Hitachi in Tennessee and Alabama at up to $40bn; TVA Clinch River and Bellefonte/Widows Creek siting is from secondary reports.

name: SII second batch: natural gas generation Pennsylvania (reported NextEra South Mon)
claim: Commerce lists gas generation in Pennsylvania at up to $17bn with offtake including co-located data centres; NextEra/South Mon 4.3 GW identification is secondary only.

name: SII second batch: natural gas generation Texas
claim: Commerce lists gas generation in Texas at up to $16bn with offtake including data centres (second batch total about $73bn).

name: SII October 2025 candidate list (Westinghouse/GE Vernova/Hitachi up to $332bn; Mitsubishi Electric AI $30bn; Panasonic storage $15bn)
claim: Announced 28 Oct 2025 as preliminary pledges in a launch phase needing review; AA lists nuclear up to $332bn, Mitsubishi Electric AI infrastructure $30bn and Panasonic energy storage $15bn.

name: SII third tranche not yet announced
claim: As of Sep 2026 Akazawa declined detail on a third tranche, with AI and semiconductor projects reported as leading candidates and no date; no third announcement found by 6 Nov 2026.

name: JBIC Japan Invest 1 LLC loan for synthetic diamond project
claim: JBIC signed a loan of about $7m to Japan Invest 1 LLC on 17 Apr 2026 (total co-financing about $23m) with NEXI insuring the private lenders' portion.

name: JBIC Japan Invest 3 LLC loan for gas generation plus data centre
claim: JBIC signed a loan of about $630m to Japan Invest 3 LLC on 17 Apr 2026 (total co-financing about $1.885bn) for a gas generation project integrated with data centre and transmission; NEXI insures private lenders; lenders unnamed.

name: JBIC Japan Invest 5 LLC loan for Texas gas generation
claim: JBIC signed about $739m (loan agreement 7 Aug 2026; total co-financing about $2.213bn) to Japan Invest 5 LLC for Texas gas generation under the Initiative; NEXI insures private loans; Citibank Tokyo agent with JPMorgan Tokyo.

name: JBIC Japan Invest 4 LLC loan and Citi-led syndicated facility (Pennsylvania gas)
source: Citi press release; search summary of JBIC release
claim: Reported: JBIC US$801m loan to JI4 signed 7 Aug 2026 with NEXI insuring a US$1.6bn private loan, and a Citi-led facility of about US$4.6bn covering JI4 and JI5; I did not open the JBIC JI4 release or the Citi page.

name: JBIC and NEXI support for US crude oil export project (JI2)
source: TXF News headline; search summary of JBIC release
claim: Search summary says JI2 received a JBIC loan co-financed with private lenders for about $415m total after amendment; article body not accessible, date and structure unverified.

name: Westinghouse / US Government / Brookfield / Cameco AP1000 partnership
claim: US government will arrange financing and permitting for at least $80bn of new Westinghouse reactors (mainly AP1000) and receives a participation interest of 20% of distributions above $17.5bn convertible to up to 20% equity; date 28 Oct 2025 per most sources (one says 27 Oct).

name: Japan support for Westinghouse AP1000 and SMRs (up to $100bn)
claim: ANS (17 Mar 2026) says the 2025 US-Japan agreement projected up to $100bn for Westinghouse reactors but specific projects were not yet identified and Westinghouse is still working transactions; a $46bn JBIC low-interest figure appears only in a secondary search summary and was not found in the ANS text.

name: TVA Clinch River BWRX-300 NRC construction permit
institution: US NRC / TVA / GE Vernova Hitachi
claim: NRC issued the first US BWRX-300 construction permit to TVA at Clinch River on 29 Sep 2026 (operating licence still required; commercial operation targeted 2033); no source found linking Japanese financing to this specific permit.

name: Lynas-JARE amended long-term rare earth supply agreement
claim: Signed 10 Mar 2026: JARE buys at least 5000 t/y PrNd at a $110/kg floor with 30% of price above $150/kg returned (capped $10m/y), at least 50% of heavy rare earths, valid to 2038; JOGMEC financing is described only as potential, not as a party.

name: Lynas $96m US DoD rare earth supply deal
claim: Trade press says Lynas signed a $96m deal with the US DoD following its expanded Japan agreement; date approximate, primary source not found.

name: Australia-Japan critical minerals joint declaration (US$1.3bn AU / US$370m JP)
institution: Government of Australia / JOGMEC / Export Finance Australia
claim: Secondary report says Australia up to $1.3bn and Japan $370m via JOGMEC for projects including Lynas; date and currency unverified.

name: US DFC / US EXIM cooperation with JBIC and NEXI (MOUs)
institution: US DFC / US EXIM / JBIC / NEXI
claim: I did not find a DFC/EXIM MOU with JBIC or NEXI in the searches run; unverified (JBIC/NEXI roles in SII are covered by E23-E26).

name: Quad Critical Minerals Initiative Framework (New Delhi)
claim: Quad foreign ministers adopted a framework to mobilise up to $20bn for secure critical-mineral supply chains; a separate July 2025 Quad initiative is mentioned only in passing and not sourced.

name: FORGE (Forum on Resource Geostrategic Engagement) and Pax Silica
claim: FORGE was unveiled at a Feb 2026 Washington ministerial with 54 nations; Pax Silica launched Dec 2025 for silicon/AI supply chains; Japan membership details and exact dates unverified.

name: US-Japan Economic 2+2 (EPC)
institution: US State / US Commerce / Japan MOFA / METI
claim: Both sides in 2024 said the 2022-launched Economic 2+2 works as an effective economic-security framework and agreed to hold it periodically; no 2026 meeting found (Feb 2026 Rubio-Motegi and Ichikawa-Rubio contacts only).

name: Alaska LNG letters of intent (JERA and Tokyo Gas)
source: Glenfarne/Tokyo Gas via Tank News; Energy Intelligence
claim: JERA (Sep 2025) and Tokyo Gas (6 Nov 2025) each signed non-binding LOIs for 1 MTPA from Alaska LNG; no binding SPA, JBIC financing or FID found, and it is not among announced SII projects.

name: Nippon Steel-US Steel golden share and investment commitments
claim: Axios (30 Jun 2026) says Nippon reaffirmed an $11bn investment pledge with allocation of $7.8bn unspecified and mostly still promised, the golden share has not been used on management decisions, and leverage rose with an S&P downgrade; the deal closed 18 Jun 2025.

name: US-Japan dispute over SII project selection and control
claim: In Feb 2026 Akazawa said the sides were far apart on first projects; Lutnick claimed Trump has complete discretion while Akazawa said selection follows the investment and consultation committees; resolved only by the 17 Feb announcement; later disputes not found.

name: DoD-MP Materials partnership (price floor and magnet offtake)
claim: DoD agreed a 10-year NdPr price floor of $110/kg (quarterly shortfall payments), 30% upside share above $110 once the 10X plant is at full capacity, and a 10-year offtake of 10X magnet output with quarterly payments of 25% of a $140M EBITDA threshold.

name: DoD equity and loan to MP Materials
claim: DoD bought $400M of Series A convertible preferred (7% PIK dividend) and extended a $150M 12-year unsecured samarium project loan; closing was set for 2025-07-11.

name: US-Japan Framework for Securing Supply of Critical Minerals and Rare Earths
source: Reporting on White House text (Mining.com; The National)
claim: Trump and Takaichi signed a framework on 2025-10-28 in Tokyo covering permitting streamlining, coordinated investment and a Supply Security Rapid Response Group led by the US Energy Secretary and Japan's METI minister.

name: US-Japan $550B investment vehicle project list (Oct 2025)
source: Japan MOF fact sheet (via search; PDF not opened)
claim: The joint fact sheet lists Japanese-linked interest of up to about $490B in 'launch phase' projects, with Lutnick saying projects still need approval and final selection rests with the US.

name: Westinghouse AP1000 and SMR fleet under Japan investment package
source: Japan MOF fact sheet (via search summary)
claim: The fact sheet lists up to $100B for Westinghouse AP1000/SMR with possible Japanese supplier involvement (MHI Toshiba IHI); CSIS cites a separate figure of $80B in a US-Westinghouse partnership.

name: GE Vernova Hitachi BWRX-300 SMR construction under Japan package
institution: GE Vernova Hitachi; Hitachi GE Vernova
source: Japan MOF fact sheet (via search summary)
claim: The fact sheet lists up to $100B for GE Vernova Hitachi BWRX-300 SMR construction with Hitachi GE Vernova as a possible Japanese participant; no funded project confirmed in my sources.

name: TVA Clinch River BWRX-300 construction permit
claim: NRC issued TVA the first US construction permit for a BWRX-300 at Clinch River on 2026-09-29; it does not authorize operation and commercial operation is reportedly targeted for 2033 (NEI Magazine; not opened).

name: Japan Steel Works forgings for GE Hitachi
institution: Japan Steel Works; GE Vernova Hitachi
claim: Energy Intelligence reportedly says GE-Hitachi sources forgings from Japan Steel Works; the date is approximate and I found no confirmed 2026 JSW or IHI contract for AP1000 forgings.

name: US heavy forging capacity gap for nuclear buildout
claim: Reporting says Westinghouse needs a 15000-tonne press for 350-tonne ingots for the largest AP1000 components and that Doosan is competing with JSW; sources conflict on supplier roles.

name: Hitachi Energy South Boston VA large power transformer plant groundbreaking
claim: Hitachi Energy broke ground on 2026-06-29 on a $457M South Boston expansion creating about 825 jobs; the site already employs about 850 and completion date was not stated on the page (other reports say 2028).

name: Hitachi $1B US grid manufacturing pledge
source: Trade press (Transformers Magazine; TDWorld) via search
claim: Hitachi Energy pledged more than $1B for US grid equipment manufacturing including the $457M South Boston plant; the announcement date was not confirmed (reported September 2025).

name: Hitachi Energy Gallman Mississippi power transformer plant
claim: Hitachi Energy is reported to commit $528M to a Gallman Mississippi power transformer plant supporting 650+ jobs, with no capacity or timeline released; primary source not opened.

name: Mitsubishi Electric Power Products Pennsylvania switchgear factory
claim: Mitsubishi Electric announced an $86M advanced switchgear factory in Western Pennsylvania in October 2024; current operating status not checked.

name: Mitsubishi Electric Memphis transformer plant
claim: Mitsubishi Electric opened a roughly $200M Memphis Tennessee transformer factory in 2013; current output and any later expansion are unchecked.

name: US power transformer deficit and import dependence
source: Wood Mackenzie press release (via search summary)
claim: Wood Mackenzie projected a 30% supply deficit for power transformers and 10% for distribution units in 2025 with imports about 80% of power transformer supply and Q2 2025 lead times of 128 weeks (GSUs 144 weeks).

name: Single US supplier of GOES
claim: Cleveland-Cliffs states Butler Works is the only US producer of regular grain-oriented electrical steel used in power and distribution transformers.

name: Cleveland-Cliffs Butler Works expansion with DOE grant
claim: A $170M Butler Works project is part funded by a $75M DOE grant and is reportedly on track for 2028; the date was not confirmed.

name: DLA GOES contract to Cleveland-Cliffs
claim: A five-year $400M award reportedly covers up to 53000 short tons of GOES from Cliffs; award date unconfirmed.

name: US Steel (Nippon Steel) Big River GOES plan
claim: Nikkei reported in November 2025 that US Steel would build GOES capability at Big River Osceola Arkansas with mass production in 2028; US Steel confirmed the project to Argus without investment or capacity details (date approximate).

name: Nippon Steel US Steel acquisition investment commitments
claim: Nippon Steel committed about $11B of new US Steel investment by 2028 (some reports cite $14B) with electrical steel mentioned mainly for automotive; whether GOES for transformers is in the formal commitments is not confirmed.

name: Furukawa Electric HVDC cable plant (Japan)
claim: Furukawa Electric will invest about JPY100bn in a Futtsu Chiba 500kV HVDC cable plant targeting 2030, a Japan-only project.

name: China April 2025 rare earth export licensing
claim: China's April 2025 licensing requirements on seven medium and heavy rare earths were never suspended and still require MOFCOM licences as of my sources; date is when the controls took effect and was not confirmed in the source.

name: China October 2025 rare earth controls suspended
claim: China formalized a one-year suspension of its 9 October 2025 expanded controls, reported to run to 2026-11-10 (a related 2024 measure suspended to 2026-11-27); I found no report of extension or reinstatement as of 2026-11-06.

name: China dual-use export ban to Japan
claim: China banned exports of dual-use items to Japanese military end users effective 2026-01-06, with reporting that medium and heavy rare earth supply to Japan was curtailed more broadly.

name: China export controls on 20 Japanese firms
claim: China prohibited dual-use exports to 20 Japanese entities it says supply Japan's military; the 2026-06 reaffirmation reported in my search is not individually sourced.

name: Lynas heavy rare earth allocation to Japan
claim: Caixin reports Lynas will reserve 75% of heavy rare earth oxide output for Japan (50% to JARE); single-source and no official Lynas or Sojitz release found.

name: Sojitz-JOGMEC additional investment in Lynas via JARE
claim: Sojitz and JOGMEC invested a further A$200M (about $132M) via JARE for up to 65% of Lynas Dy/Tb output, roughly 30% of Japan's heavy rare earth demand; reported in 2023, exact date not captured.

name: Lynas Seadrift Texas heavy rare earth plant
claim: Lynas said in August 2025 it was negotiating a DoD offtake for Seadrift output on commercial terms and flagged uncertainty over whether the plant would proceed; I found no 2026 status.

name: Shin-Etsu new rare earth refinery in Fukui
claim: Shin-Etsu announced a new rare earth plant in Fukui, its first new Japanese refinery in about two decades (a figure of about $220M appears only in an unverified aggregator).

name: Japanese magnet makers US production (Shin-Etsu TDK Proterial Daido)
claim: I found no confirmed US magnet plant for TDK Proterial or Daido (Proterial's recent expansion is a $225M India plant) and the sources on Shin-Etsu US sites conflict.

name: Energy Fuels-Vulcan Elements rare earth oxide MOU
claim: Energy Fuels and Vulcan signed an MOU for NdPr and Dy oxide supply from Q4 2025 with long-term agreements to be negotiated; no Japanese participant found.

name: Panasonic Energy De Soto Kansas plant opening
claim: Panasonic opened the De Soto plant in July 2025 with about 1100 employees and one of eight lines running versus a 4000-job target.

name: Panasonic De Soto shift toward data-center batteries
claim: Panasonic plans to repurpose some US lines including De Soto to data-center energy storage with first cells expected mid-to-late 2028 or early 2029 while EV cell output continues; ramp is slower than planned.

name: Toyota Battery Manufacturing North Carolina
claim: Toyota began production at its Liberty NC battery plant on 2025-11-12 (reported investment $13.9B with a further $10B pledged); output is mainly hybrid batteries and sources differ on line counts.

name: Honda-LG Ohio JV building sale to Honda
claim: LGES agreed to sell the Ohio JV factory building and related assets to Honda for about $2.85B with the JV continuing via lease and closing targeted for 2026-02-28; I did not verify that it closed.

name: AESC South Carolina plant construction paused
claim: AESC paused its $1.6B Florence County plant in June 2025 citing policy and market uncertainty; ownership is described variously as Yokohama-headquartered or Chinese-owned and I did not resolve this.

name: Toyota Tsusho-LGES North America battery recycling JV
claim: Toyota Tsusho and LGES agreed in June 2025 to form a North Carolina battery recycling JV expected to start operating in 2026; date approximate and status unchecked.

name: Toyota-Sumitomo Metal Mining solid-state cathode development
claim: Toyota and SMM agreed in October 2025 to co-develop solid-state cathode material with mass production planned for 2028; the project is in Japan and I found no US plant.

name: Rapidus-IBM 2nm cooperation
claim: IBM supplies 2nm process technology to Rapidus with Rapidus engineers at IBM Albany and Rapidus targeting mass production in 2H 2027; subsidy totals vary by source.

name: SB Energy Portsmouth Ohio gas plant under Japan fund
claim: One of the first three funded projects under the $550B vehicle is a $33B 9.2GW SB Energy gas plant in Portsmouth Ohio; I could not confirm the other two projects or the exact date.

name: US-Australia Critical Minerals Framework
claim: Trump and Albanese signed a framework in October 2025 with a priority pipeline of about US$8.5B and a joint Supply Security Response Group; Japan is not a party.

name: Alcoa-Sojitz Wagerup gallium project
institution: Alcoa; Sojitz; Japan govt; US Dept of War
claim: The trilateral Wagerup gallium project reportedly involves Sojitz and the Japanese government with an estimated $174M US Dept of War equity investment and groundbreaking on 2026-08-24; the equity announcement year is unclear.

name: JBIC loan to Rincon lithium project
claim: A March 2026 JBIC loan to Rincon Mining in Australia is co-financed with private banks IFC and EFA and DFC is not named; the URL is a 2025 JBIC release that I did not confirm matches this loan.

name: DFC-JBIC cooperation MOU renewal
claim: DFC and JBIC renewed their bilateral MOU covering critical-minerals supply chains and energy transition investment; the renewal date was not captured.

name: Philippines DOF-JBIC energy partnership renewal
claim: DOF and JBIC renewed an energy and infrastructure partnership in October 2026; no US co-financing or nuclear/minerals component confirmed.

name: US-EU Joint Statement on a Framework on an Agreement on Reciprocal, Fair and Balanced Trade (EU-level, applies to Germany)
claim: US applies the higher of MFN or a 15% all-in tariff on EU goods; the EU intends US$750bn of US LNG, oil and nuclear purchases through 2028 and US$40bn of AI chips, and European firms are expected to invest US$600bn more in the US; commitments mostly non-binding.

name: US Section 232 treatment of EU autos, pharmaceuticals, semiconductors and lumber under the framework (EU-level, applies to Germany)
claim: Joint statement caps combined MFN plus Section 232 at 15% for EU pharmaceuticals, semiconductors and lumber, and applies a combined 15% to EU autos and parts (conditional on the EU tabling its tariff legislation); steel and aluminium left to possible tariff-rate quotas.

name: EU legislation implementing the US-EU deal: tariff cuts on US industrial goods (EU-level, applies to Germany)
institution: European Parliament / Council of the EU
claim: Parliament approved the main regulation on 16 Jun 2026 (440-151), governments adopted it on 25 Jun and EU tariff cuts took effect 1 Jul 2026; Parliament's position carried suspension and sunset clauses (sunset 31 Mar 2028); final clause text not checked.

name: European Parliament freeze of the US-EU deal over Greenland threats (EU-level, applies to Germany)
claim: Parliament suspended work on approving the deal on 21 Jan 2026 over US Greenland demands and tariff threats and unfroze it in early Feb 2026; the freeze is lifted, so status shown is historical.

name: Supreme Court IEEPA ruling and Section 122 surcharge on EU goods (EU-level, applies to Germany)
claim: Supreme Court held on 20 Feb 2026 that IEEPA does not authorise tariffs; a Section 122 surcharge (reported at 10%, then 15%) ran from 24 Feb for 150 days and could exceed the Turnberry 15% ceiling where MFN is zero (Bruegel); it expired 24 Jul 2026; sources conflict on the rate.

name: Section 301 forced-labour tariffs replacing Section 122 (applies to EU goods incl. Germany)
claim: New Section 301 tariffs of roughly 10-12.5% on about 60 economies took effect 24 Jul 2026 as Section 122 expired, and USTR said deal caps for the EU and Japan would be upheld; EU-specific rate and 15% all-in treatment not confirmed in a primary source.

name: US Section 232 steel, aluminium and copper tariffs and derivatives (EU-level, applies to Germany)
claim: April 2026 proclamation sets 50% on core steel, aluminium and copper codes and 25% on derivatives from 6 Apr; the EU contests derivative coverage and no EU tariff-rate quota was confirmed in force; EU-specific treatment unverified.

name: EU rebalancing countermeasures on EUR 93bn of US goods, suspended without end date (EU-level, applies to Germany)
claim: On 31 Jul 2026 the Commission removed the 6 Aug expiry and extended indefinitely the suspension of EUR 93bn of countermeasures (Regulation 2025/1564), under continuous review with the option to reactivate; page seen only as a search result.

name: US-EU memorandum of understanding on a critical minerals strategic partnership (EU-level, applies to Germany)
claim: Rubio and Sefcovic signed a non-binding MOU on 24 Apr 2026 to diversify mining, processing and refining and coordinate on third-country export controls; a USTR action plan explores border-adjusted price floors and a later plurilateral club; no binding agreement or projects found.

name: EU-US Trade and Technology Council (EU-level, applies to Germany)
claim: TTC (created 2021) had its future questioned under the 2025 administration; no formal termination or revival was found, so it is treated as dormant and superseded by the 2025 framework and 2026 critical minerals MOU.

name: G7 Critical Minerals Action Plan
claim: G7 leaders (including the USA and Germany) launched the Action Plan at Kananaskis on 17 Jun 2025 to diversify production, encourage investment and local value creation; interested members support the Minerals Security Partnership; no named German-US projects.

name: Minerals Security Partnership (MSP) and MSP Forum
claim: Germany and the USA are both original MSP partners and automatic members of the MSP Forum launched in 2024; membership read from a Sep 2024 news item and a current list was not checked.

name: US-Germany Climate and Energy Partnership (hydrogen, LNG, offshore wind)
institution: German economy ministry / US Department of State
claim: Germany and the US signed an energy and climate partnership in May 2022 with work on LNG, hydrogen and offshore wind; no 2025-26 bilateral energy, hydrogen or critical-minerals agreement was found, and current activity is unconfirmed.

name: KfW Raw Materials Fund first investments (Vulcan EUR 150m, Arafura EUR 50m)
claim: KfW's Raw Materials Fund (part of the Germany Fund) made its first two equity decisions, EUR 150m in Vulcan Energy (lithium) and EUR 50m in Arafura's Nolans rare earths project; a third is in due diligence and the target size is EUR 1.5bn; no US-linked project named; USD at about 1.16 per EUR.

name: Siemens AG US investment pledge of more than US$10bn
claim: Siemens announced more than US$10bn of added US investment in March 2025, including electrical-products plants in Fort Worth and Pomona (US$285m reported) and the Altair acquisition; the figure combines capex and an acquisition.

name: Siemens Energy large power transformer plant, Charlotte NC
claim: Siemens Energy announced a US$150m large power transformer plant in Charlotte in Feb 2024, originally for early-2026 output (24 units a year, rising to 57); a June 2025 report put US production at 2027; current start date not confirmed.

name: Siemens Energy US$1bn US grid and turbine manufacturing expansion incl. Mississippi switchgear plant
claim: Siemens Energy announced US$1bn of US expansion across transformers, grid equipment and turbines, with a greenfield high-voltage switchgear plant in Mississippi (up to 300 jobs); announcement day and project-level amounts not confirmed.

name: e-VAC Magnetics NdFeB permanent magnet plant, Sumter SC (Vacuumschmelze)
claim: German-owned VAC's Sumter plant (about US$500m, nearly 2,000 t/yr, operating since late 2025) shipped first magnets and held an opening ceremony in July 2026; about 90% of output was contracted to GM; expansion room reported up to 12,000 t.

name: GM termination of strategic sourcing agreement with e-VAC (Vacuumschmelze)
claim: GM terminated its long-term magnet supply agreement with e-VAC (reported 22 Oct 2026); the parties are reportedly in arbitration and the dispute dates from April 2026; one German source dates the notice to July 2026; reasons not stated by the parties.

name: Energy Fuels acquisition of Vacuumschmelze (VAC) for about US$1.9bn
claim: US-listed Energy Fuels agreed on 23 Jun 2026 to buy 100% of Hanau-based VAC from Ara Partners (US$718m cash plus shares); close expected early 2027 subject to US and European approvals; price may adjust with the GM arbitration.

name: e-VAC US$112m advanced manufacturing tax credit for Sumter plant
claim: e-VAC was awarded about US$112m in Section 48C tax credits for its US$500m-plus Sumter facility in April 2024; current status of the credit not checked.

name: Aurubis Richmond multimetal recycling plant, Augusta GA
source: Recycling Today; SMM; Augusta Business Daily
claim: Aurubis's Augusta melt shop is producing recycled-content metals and a second module lifts capacity to 180,000 t/yr, with expansion completion expected Sep 2026 (not confirmed done); the US$800m figure is from a secondary source; publication date approximate.

name: BMW Spartanburg SC: iX5 electric production and Woodruff battery pack plant
claim: BMW's US$1.7bn US programme includes a roughly US$700m Woodruff pack plant using Gen6 cylindrical cells from AESC (Florence SC) and iX5 production at Spartanburg, with series pack output reported for Dec 2026; publication date approximate.

name: Mercedes-Benz Tuscaloosa AL new model and VW/Scout Motors South Carolina plant
claim: Mercedes plans a new Tuscaloosa model by 2027 (GLC localisation reported later); VW's Scout plant in South Carolina (about US$2bn) targets EV SUVs and pickups from late 2026-2027, while ID.4 output at Chattanooga was reported ending April 2026; sources conflict.

name: Tesla Giga Berlin-Brandenburg (Gruenheide) 4680 cell expansion to 18 GWh
claim: US-owned Tesla raised planned on-site 4680 cell capacity at Gruenheide from 8 to 18 GWh a year with about US$250m, cell output from H1 2027; the plant currently uses CATL and LG Energy Solution cells.

name: Infineon sale of Austin Fab 25 to SkyWater with supply agreement
claim: Infineon agreed in Feb 2025 to sell its 200 mm Austin fab to SkyWater with a long-term supply agreement, reducing its own US wafer capacity (about 4,000 US staff remain); closing status and any new US investment not confirmed.

name: SGL Carbon synthetic graphite: no confirmed US anode capacity
source: MarketBeat (SGL Q4 call summary); SGL Carbon
claim: SGL's anode funding found is European (EUR 42.9m IPCEI, Meitingen); the March 2026 call summary reports it closed Lavradio and idled Moses Lake in 2025 (a carbon-fibre site); no 2026 US anode plant or US offtake was found.

name: RCEP in force for Japan and Korea
source: METI; Japan Customs; Australian Border Force
claim: RCEP entered into force for Japan on 1 Jan 2022 and for Korea on 1 Feb 2022, giving the two countries a shared preferential trade framework with no separate bilateral FTA; tariff schedules not reviewed.

name: Korea's CPTPP accession: no formal application
claim: In June 2026 Korea's trade ministry said no decision had been made on applying to CPTPP after reports of a late-June application; Japan reportedly would back accession without first requiring Korea to lift its Fukushima seafood ban; the Japan position is a press report.

name: Lee says CPTPP entry unlikely in his term
claim: A Reuters headline of 26 Oct 2026 reports President Lee Jae-myung said Korea is unlikely to join the CPTPP within his term; only the headline was read, so wording and reasons are unconfirmed.

name: 2019 Japanese export controls on three semiconductor and display materials
claim: From July 2019 Japan required individual licences for fluorinated polyimide, photoresist and hydrogen fluoride exports to Korea and removed Korea from its white list; Korea removed Japan from its own list in Aug 2019 and filed a WTO complaint; Japan lifted the three-item curbs in Mar 2023.

name: Korean chipmakers' dependence on Japanese materials (2019 estimate)
claim: Press coverage of the 2019 dispute put Japan's share of the three controlled materials used by Korean chipmakers at about 90% for fluorinated polyimide and photoresist and about 70% for hydrogen fluoride; figures are as quoted by media and not checked against customs data.

name: Korea withdraws WTO complaint over Japan's export curbs
claim: Korea completed procedures to drop its 2019 WTO complaint on 23 Mar 2023, a week after the 16 Mar Yoon-Kishida summit; Japan had pledged to lift the three-material curbs; the article does not confirm the curbs had by then been lifted.

name: White-list restoration, both sides (2023)
claim: Korea restored Japan to its white list in April 2023; Japan announced on 27 Jun 2023 that Korea would be restored to its list effective 21 Jul 2023, ending the 2019 white-list exclusions; the Apr 2023 Korean step is from the same article.

name: Yoon-Kishida summit and normalisation (Tokyo, 16 Mar 2023)
claim: The 16 Mar 2023 Tokyo summit restored shuttle diplomacy, with Japan pledging to lift its three-material curbs and Korea to drop its WTO case; resumption of the economic-security and supply-chain channels was reported separately and not checked.

name: Camp David trilateral supply-chain early warning system (18 Aug 2023)
source: Mayer Brown (on White House fact sheet)
claim: The three leaders agreed to pilot an early warning system exchanging supply-chain information via embassies in selected countries, with critical minerals and rechargeable batteries as priority products, plus an annual commerce and industry ministers track; the system is not published as operating beyond the pilot.

name: US-Japan-ROK senior officials agree to deepen critical minerals dialogue (Sept 2025)
claim: Senior officials meeting in New York agreed to enhance dialogue on critical minerals and cooperation in Southeast Asia and Sub-Saharan Africa through the trilateral Early Warning System; read from a search summary and not from an official statement.

name: Critical Minerals Ministerial, Washington (Feb 2026); Korea chairs FORGE
claim: The US-hosted ministerial in Feb 2026 was attended by Japan and Korea among others, and Korea was reported to chair the FORGE critical-minerals forum through June 2026; exact meeting date and FORGE membership not confirmed.

name: 1st Korea-Japan Mineral Resources Cooperation Dialogue (Tokyo)
claim: Korean and Japanese officials agreed a close cooperation system on critical-mineral supply risks, support for company and agency cooperation on joint development in third countries (Latin America, Asia, Africa), and policy coordination in the Minerals Security Partnership and IEA; no projects were named.

name: 2nd Korea-Japan Mineral Resources Cooperation Dialogue
claim: The second round discussed a joint response to falling copper treatment and refining charges, cooperation within the Minerals Security Partnership and ways to develop critical minerals jointly in third countries; no agreement or named project was reported.

name: Japan-ROK Hydrogen and Ammonia Cooperation Dialogue (2nd meeting)
source: Search summary of METI release (page returned 403)
claim: The dialogue, set up Feb 2024 with a first meeting in Jun 2024, held its second meeting in Tokyo on 26 Mar 2025 and agreed to develop a Japan-ROK cooperation platform for hydrogen and ammonia supply chains; the METI page could not be opened.

name: Lee-Takaichi summit, Nara: economic-security talks agreed
claim: On 13 Jan 2026 the leaders discussed supply-chain cooperation in depth and agreed to launch agency-level talks on economic security cooperation, with rare-earth stabilisation reported as a focus; no outputs were published.

name: Korea-Japan Supply Chain Partnership Arrangement (SCPA)
claim: Ministers Kim Jung-kwan and Akazawa signed the SCPA in Tokyo on 14 Mar 2026: early notification of disruptions, an emergency meeting within five days of a request, and prior consultation before measures that could harm the other side; no amounts or named projects.

name: Korea-Japan Industrial and Trade Policy Dialogue launched
claim: A standing consultative body launched 14 Mar 2026 to review trade cooperation, economic security, supply chains, steel and mineral resources; the same article reports plans for joint exploration and investment in critical minerals and shared market monitoring; no schedule published.

name: METI-MOTIE export control policy dialogue (March 2026)
claim: A bilateral export-control policy dialogue was reported for 14-16 Mar 2026 alongside the ministerial; the date and agenda come from a search summary and were not read on the page.

name: KOGAS-JERA LNG supply cooperation agreement (with swaps)
claim: KOGAS and JERA signed an LNG supply cooperation agreement in Tokyo on 14 Mar 2026 including LNG swaps and a framework for joint response to future supply crises; no volumes or value reported.

name: Lee-Takaichi summit, Andong, and energy-security joint press release
claim: The 19 May 2026 trade-ministry release covers crude oil swaps and mutual supply in a crisis, deeper LNG cooperation under the KOGAS-JERA agreement, SCPA crisis mechanisms and regional reserves via Japan's proposed POWERR Asia; no projects or funding named; hydrogen and critical minerals not covered.

name: SCPA implementation meeting in Tokyo (Sept 2026)
claim: A trade-press summary reports a 2 Sept 2026 implementation meeting covering critical-mineral diversification, emergency energy supply and regulatory coordination; the page was not opened and no other source corroborates it.

name: 33rd Korea-Japan Business Conference (FKI-Keidanren), Seoul
claim: The joint statement backs coordination on resource procurement and supply-chain stability, support for Korea's CPTPP accession, hydrogen certification and safety standards, critical-mineral stockpiling and crisis response through the SCPA, and an early resumption of the Korea-US-Japan Business Dialogue; business statement, not binding.

name: 32nd Korea-Japan Business Conference, Tokyo: CPTPP support
claim: At the October 2025 Tokyo conference the two business federations agreed Korea's CPTPP participation was important given US protectionism and supply-chain disruption; read from a search summary only.

name: KNOC-JOGMEC MOU on hydrogen, ammonia and CCS (Feb 2025)
claim: KNOC reportedly signed an MOU with JOGMEC in February 2025 on cooperation in hydrogen, ammonia and CCS; the article was surfaced by search and not opened. No JOGMEC-KOMIR mineral agreement was found.

name: JERA-Samsung C&T MoU on hydrogen and ammonia value chains
claim: JERA and Samsung C&T signed a two-year initial MoU on 6 Jul 2026 to explore resilience and supply security in hydrogen and ammonia value chains, including storage and ammonia trading; exploratory, no amounts.

name: JERA-Lotte Fine Chemical low-carbon ammonia and hydrogen collaboration
claim: JERA and Lotte Fine Chemical agreed in Aug 2024 to develop low-carbon hydrogen and ammonia fuel supply chains, with joint studies on commercial frameworks and ammonia bunkering at Yokohama; current status not confirmed.

name: OCI-Tokuyama semiconductor-grade polysilicon JV, Sarawak
claim: OCI and Tokuyama hold 50:50 in OCI Tokuyama Semiconductor Materials, which broke ground in Sarawak in July 2025 on an 8,000 tonne a year plant targeting commercial operation in 2029; semiconductor-grade, not solar-grade; amount not stated.

name: Toyota-LGES long-term battery supply agreement, US
claim: LGES agreed to supply Toyota's North American EVs with about 20 GWh a year of modules from 2025, with roughly 4 trillion won (about 3 billion dollars) invested in Michigan lines dedicated to Toyota; contract value not disclosed, later changes not checked.

name: Honda-LGES L-H Battery joint venture, Ohio: building sold to Honda
claim: The 2023 Honda-LGES joint venture L-H Battery keeps operating its Ohio cell plant under a lease after LGES sold the building to Honda for about 4.22 trillion won (2.85 billion dollars) announced Dec 2025; a later report of a lower closing value of 3.74 trillion won is unconfirmed.

name: Samsung Advanced Package Lab, Yokohama
claim: Samsung's advanced-packaging R&D lab opened in Yokohama's Minato Mirai district in Sept 2026 per a Herald report, after a Dec 2023 plan of about 40 billion yen (280 million dollars); investment figures vary across reports and Japanese materials makers are named partners.

name: Sumitomo Chemical plans photoresist production in Korea
claim: Sumitomo Chemical plans EUV and ArF photoresist production in Korea, previously made only in Osaka, with about 30 billion yen invested across Korea and Japan; site and start date undecided; dollar figure is a rough conversion.

name: Japanese separator suppliers to LG Energy Solution
claim: A 2024 report says LGES sources separators from China's SEMCORP and Senior and from Japan's Asahi Kasei and Toray, while Samsung SDI relies mainly on Korea's WCP; no Korea-based Japanese separator plant was found in 2025-26 coverage.

name: Korea's higher dependence on Chinese NdFeB magnets than Japan
claim: A 2023 KED Global analysis put Korea's dependence on Chinese neodymium permanent magnets at 88% versus 31% for Japan; no Japanese magnet-maker plant or supply deal for Korea was found in this research.

name: Australia-US Free Trade Agreement (AUSFTA)
claim: AUSFTA is in force with a Joint Committee supervising implementation and committees on goods, agriculture and SPS; it gave no exemption from the 2025-26 US tariffs; entry-into-force date not stated on the page

name: US-Australia Climate, Critical Minerals and Clean Energy Transformation Compact
claim: Signed 20 May 2023; set up a Clean Energy Industrial Transformation forum and a ministerial Taskforce on Critical Minerals led by Industry, Science and Resources and the US NSC; no dollar amounts

name: Quad Critical Minerals Initiative
claim: Launched July 2025 and framework adopted May 2026 to mobilise up to US$20bn of public and private support for mining, processing and recycling; no project list; leaders' summit date not confirmed

name: US-Australia Framework for Securing of Supply in the Mining and Processing of Critical Minerals and Rare Earths
claim: Signed 20 Oct 2025; each government to provide at least US$1bn within six months toward a US$8.5bn pipeline of priority projects in both countries; creates a Supply Security Response Group; release names no price floor

name: US-Australia Critical Minerals Supply Security Response Group and investment ministerial
source: Metal Tech News; Department of Energy
claim: The Response Group was established in March 2026 after a Tokyo investment ministerial on 14 March; the US launched the FORGE forum in February 2026; the group's outputs and meeting record are not published in these sources

name: Alcoa-Sojitz Wagerup gallium recovery project
claim: Australia offered up to US$200m concessional equity with an offtake right and the US also takes equity with an offtake right; trilateral with Japan, which has funded 50% of costs; could supply up to 10% of world gallium

name: US Department of War equity in Alcoa gallium project
claim: DoW announced an estimated US$174m equity financing on 31 Aug 2026 after groundbreaking on 24 Aug; the plant is designed for 100 t a year of gallium; secondary report, DoW release not read

name: Australian equity in Arafura Nolans rare earths project
claim: A US$100m Australian equity investment in the Nolans project in the Northern Territory, expected to supply about 5% of world rare earths once operating; US side of financing not stated in the release

name: Arafura Nolans construction start and final investment decision
claim: Final investment decision in May 2026 after an Australian offtake commitment under the Strategic Reserve; construction began 8 Oct 2026; credit agencies from the US, Canada, Korea and Germany support it; the article's A$1.2bn figure is ambiguous

name: EXIM letters of interest for Australian projects
claim: At signing EXIM issued seven non-binding letters of interest totalling over US$2.2bn, including Northern Minerals, Graphinex and La Trobe Magnesium; these are preliminary and not finalised loans

name: EXIM and Export Finance Australia coordinated letters for Ardea nickel and Tronox rare earth refinery
claim: In April 2026 EXIM and EFA issued coordinated letters for up to about US$1bn for Ardea Resources' Kalgoorlie nickel project and about US$849m for Tronox's rare earths refinery; letters are not committed loans; exact date not given

name: Office of Strategic Capital conditional loan for Sunrise Energy Metals Syerston scandium
claim: OSC announced a conditional commitment of up to US$400m for a proposed 25-year loan to Sunrise Energy Metals' Syerston scandium project in New South Wales, subject to conditions; August date approximate

name: Lynas-Department of War rare earth oxide supply letter of intent with NdPr floor price
claim: Lynas USA signed a binding letter of intent for DoW to buy about US$96m of light and heavy rare earth oxides over four years with a US$110/kg NdPr floor, replacing the earlier Seadrift-linked arrangement; final supply terms and tonnages not stated

name: Lynas Seadrift Texas heavy rare earths plant
claim: Lynas has said there is significant uncertainty whether Seadrift will be built and in what form, and supplies the US from Malaysia; the March 2026 DoW deal replaced the Seadrift-linked purchase; no cancellation or construction start confirmed

name: Export Finance Australia loan for Iluka Eneabba rare earths refinery
claim: Australia's non-recourse loan to Iluka totals A$1.65bn after a A$400m top-up in May 2026, with commissioning planned mid-2027; the loan is Australian-funded and no US offtake or EXIM role was found; May date approximate

name: Australian Critical Minerals Strategic Reserve
claim: A$1.2bn (about US$840m) reserve using offtake rights, with Arafura an early offtake; the Bill gives Export Finance Australia the tools; price-stabilisation design not published; US counterpart is the US$12bn Project Vault; operations expected H2 2026 per secondary sources

name: Future Made in Australia Critical Minerals Production Tax Incentive
claim: Law since February 2025: a 10% refundable offset on processing costs for 31 critical minerals, claimable up to 10 years for production between 1 Jul 2027 and 30 Jun 2040; uranium was removed from eligibility by amendment; the uranium point is from a secondary summary

name: Section 122 interim US tariff on Australia (10%)
claim: After the Supreme Court struck down IEEPA tariffs on 20 Feb 2026, a 10% Section 122 surcharge applied to Australian goods from 24 Feb for 150 days and lapsed on 24 Jul 2026; AUSFTA gave no exemption

name: Section 301 forced-labor tariff on Australia (12.5%)
claim: From 24 Jul 2026 most Australian goods face a 12.5% Section 301 forced-labor tariff because Australia has no forced-labour import ban, versus 10% for economies with one; some exports reportedly exempt; one source disagrees on the band; Federal Register schedule not read

name: Section 232 tariffs on steel, aluminium, copper and autos apply to Australia
claim: Section 232 tariffs on steel, aluminium, copper and automobiles continued unchanged beside the Section 122 and Section 301 measures; Australia-specific rates, quotas or exemptions were not found

name: AUKUS submarine industrial base contribution
claim: Australia's US$3bn contribution to the US submarine industrial base funded Electric Boat's first AUKUS contract in April 2026; sources differ on how much has been paid and on whether Australia is assured a Virginia-class boat; no clean-energy supply link identified

name: Albemarle idles Kemerton lithium hydroxide plant
claim: US-based Albemarle idled its last Kemerton, Western Australia lithium hydroxide train in February 2026 after putting Train 2 on care and maintenance in 2024; Greenbushes and Wodgina stakes are unaffected

name: Covalent Kwinana lithium hydroxide refinery enters production
claim: The 50,000 t/yr Kwinana refinery moved into production in October 2025 and is preparing samples for customer qualification; no US offtake or US investor was found for it or for other Australian lithium chemical plants

name: GLE-Silex Paducah laser enrichment facility
claim: The NRC released a final environmental impact statement for GLE's Paducah, Kentucky laser enrichment plant, majority owned by Australian-listed Silex, with a DOE agreement to re-enrich depleted tails; no construction start or Australian government finance shown

name: Korea-US Free Trade Agreement (KORUS)
claim: KORUS has been in force since March 2012; amended in 2018 on autos, light trucks and investment rules without congressional action; the countries still use its consultative mechanisms; exact day of entry into force not stated in the source

name: US-Korea Joint Fact Sheet on the trade and investment deal
source: Korea Times (full text of joint fact sheet)
claim: Sets a 15% US tariff on Korean goods (higher of KORUS, MFN or 15%), 15% Section 232 on autos and parts, no more than 15% on pharma, semiconductors no less favourable than comparable partners; commits US$350bn (US$200bn plus US$150bn shipbuilding) with a US$20bn annual cap; reproduced text, not the whitehouse.gov page

name: MOU on US-Korea Strategic Investment
claim: Lutnick and Minister Kim signed the MOU on the US$200bn strategic-investment tranche, capped at US$20bn a year; reported profit split is 50:50 until principal and interest are repaid, then 10:90 in the US favour; the MOU text itself was not read

name: US$150bn shipbuilding investment (MASGA)
claim: The US$150bn shipbuilding half of the pledge is to be financed through direct investment, guarantees and loans led by Korean policy-finance institutions; reports say Hanwha Philly Shipyard expansion is delayed because the fund has not taken concrete shape; article date not shown

name: Hanwha Philly Shipyard first US Navy shipbuilding order
claim: Hanwha reportedly won its first US Navy shipbuilding contract since buying Philly Shipyard in December 2024, worth about US$269m (KRW 357.5bn), with construction at the Philadelphia yard; not tied to MASGA fund disbursement in the source

name: Korea Special Act on investment in the United States
claim: Assembly passed the act on 12 Mar 2026 (226-8-8), creating the Korea-US Strategic Investment Corporation with KRW 2tn (about US$1.36bn) paid-in capital and prior-report rather than prior-approval oversight; effective 18 Jun 2026

name: First Korea-US strategic investment projects (Texas gas, Alaska LNG, nuclear)
claim: Joint statement of 1 Oct 2026 formalises three projects: Encinal, Texas 6.3 GW gas plant (US$22.3bn), Alaska LNG (over US$50bn expected, subject to commercial reasonableness) and nuclear (up to US$120bn); the annual cap and vehicle structure are not addressed in this article

name: US nuclear build-out under the Korean investment pledge (eight reactors)
claim: Up to US$120bn for eight US reactors (US$100bn construction, US$20bn contingency), with a US$10bn advance payment for long-lead items targeted by year-end 2026; links to the May 2025 goal of 10 large reactors under construction by 2030; reactor designs not specified in this article

name: Korean minority stake in Westinghouse
claim: Korean companies will pursue a significant minority stake in Westinghouse to share gains from large-reactor projects, with terms to be set in commercial talks; other reports put it at 5 to 10 percent but that figure is not in this source

name: US-Korea 123 Agreement revision, enrichment and reprocessing talks
claim: Fact sheet states US support for a process toward Korean civil enrichment and reprocessing, subject to the 123 Agreement and US law, and approves nuclear-powered submarines; formal talks reportedly began June 2026 and were still discussing 123 revision in September 2026; no revision signed

name: Westinghouse-KEPCO/KHNP global settlement
claim: Westinghouse, KEPCO and KHNP settled their APR1400 intellectual-property dispute on 16 Jan 2025, dismissing all legal actions and setting up future cooperation on projects worldwide; terms are confidential, so market-allocation reports cannot be confirmed

name: IEEPA ruling and Section 122 interim tariff on Korea
claim: After the Supreme Court ruling the President lifted the EO 14257 tariffs, including Korea's 15% country rate, on 20 Feb 2026 and imposed a temporary 10% global tariff under Section 122, which expired in July 2026; refund treatment not covered

name: Section 301 forced-labor tariff on Korea (12.5%)
claim: On 23 Jul 2026 the US imposed a 12.5% tariff on most Korean goods after a Section 301 forced-labor investigation; a separate excess-capacity Section 301 probe could add tariffs and Seoul wants assurance the total stays within the agreed 15%

name: Section 232 autos and auto parts at 15% for Korea
claim: Korean autos and parts face a 15% Section 232 rate (combined with MFN) under the November 2025 deal, applied retroactively to 1 Nov 2025 for autos per implementing guidance; Section 232 is unaffected by the IEEPA ruling; Federal Register notice not opened

name: Section 232 steel and aluminium tariffs on Korea
claim: Tariffs on most Korean steel and aluminium imports remain at 50%; the fact sheet does not address them and the earlier steel quota was terminated in 2025

name: Section 232 semiconductor tariff and Korean treatment
claim: The deal caps future Section 232 chip tariffs for Korea, subject to talks; trade press reports a January 2026 25% Section 232 tariff on certain advanced chips with Korean memory exports to data centres largely exempt; scope and exemption not confirmed in a primary source

name: Section 232 polysilicon tariff and minimum import price
claim: Proclamation of 6 Aug 2026 sets a 15% tariff on certain derivatives and minimum import prices on polysilicon and derivatives from 4 Dec 2026; Korea's combined rate is capped at 15% under the deal; dates and scope taken from secondary summaries

name: Coupang Section 301 petition and Korean digital-regulation friction
claim: A January 2026 Section 301 petition targets Korea's treatment of Coupang, on which USTR has not acted; a July 2026 House Judiciary interim report called it discriminatory; the US also criticises the pace of Korean investment; reported January 2026 threat of 25% tariffs not in this source

name: Hyundai-LG Energy Solution Georgia battery plant immigration raid
claim: ICE detained 475 people at the US$4.3bn Georgia plant in September 2025, many Korean technicians on visa issues; Hyundai said opening slipped two to three months and reports in April 2026 said it was ready to open; actual production start not confirmed

name: Section 45X credit and foreign-entity (FEOC) restrictions for battery makers
claim: Section 45X advanced-manufacturing credit remains available to Korean plants but foreign-entity sourcing limits have applied since 1 Jan 2026, pushing Korean makers toward non-Chinese materials; current credit rates, phase-out and the 85% threshold seen in one source were not confirmed

name: Hanwha Qcells Cartersville ingot-wafer-cell-module plant
claim: Qcells began cell manufacturing at Cartersville, Georgia; by Q3 2026 it expects 3.3 GW each of ingot, wafer and cell and 3.5 GW of modules there, plus 5.1 GW modules at Dalton; ingot and wafer status not stated; investment not disclosed; a secondary report cites US$675m of 2026 AMPC

name: Korean polysilicon supply to Hanwha Qcells and US tariff exposure
claim: Korea's trade ministry asked Washington for flexible treatment in the polysilicon probe, saying Hanwha Qcells and OCI avoid cheap Chinese polysilicon, with Qcells sourcing mainly from OCI's Malaysian plants; US-to-Korea polysilicon volumes are not documented in this source

name: LG Energy Solution Michigan LFP storage-cell line
claim: LGES began mass production of LFP storage cells by repurposing part of its Holland, Michigan EV plant, targeting over 30 GWh by end-2026; a US$1.6bn LFP supply deal with DTE Energy is reported; Arizona plant timing not confirmed; publication date approximate

name: Samsung SDI Indiana storage-cell output and US$1bn ESS supply deal
claim: Samsung SDI secured a KRW 1.5tn (about US$1bn) US ESS cell supply deal, starting with NCA before LFP; its Kokomo, Indiana line was reported starting ESS output in 2026; the StarPlus (Stellantis) and BlueOval SK joint ventures were not covered; date approximate

name: Korean cathode material supply to US battery plants
claim: POSCO Future M began cathode exports to the US in October 2025 and its GM joint venture Ultium CAM is in Quebec; no Korean cathode plant on US soil was confirmed in this search; L&F targets North American LFP supply by end Q3 2026; EcoPro not found

name: POSCO International-ReElement rare earth and magnet joint venture
claim: A US$200m JV, run by POSCO International as largest shareholder with ReElement refining technology, plans US NdPr-Dy-Tb oxides then magnets and motor cores, following a September 2025 MOU; site and offtake not confirmed here; no MP Materials link found

name: Korea Zinc Crucible smelter, Clarksville Tennessee, with US government equity
institution: Korea Zinc / Department of War / Commerce
claim: Multi-metal smelter project of about US$7.4bn through Crucible JV, with the Department of War reported as largest shareholder at 40% (US$760m in one account, US$1.4bn conditional in another) and a US$210m Commerce grant; copper capacity not confirmed; stake closing not confirmed

name: US restriction on black mass exports
claim: A Korean report says the US has restricted exports of black mass and tungsten scrap since 27 Aug 2025, so US-origin recycling feed is unavailable to Korean recyclers; issuing authority and scope not confirmed in a primary source

name: SK On-Westwater conditional natural graphite offtake
claim: SK On signed a conditional offtake with US graphite developer Westwater for battery-grade natural graphite in North America; the article is from 2024 and current status was not checked

name: HD Hyundai Electric second Alabama transformer plant
claim: Second Montgomery, Alabama plant (312,000 sq ft, about US$200m) due for completion in April and to lift extra-high-voltage transformer capacity about 50%, up to 765 kV; completion year inferred; other outlets give US$273.7m across Ulsan and Alabama

name: Hyosung Heavy Industries Memphis transformer expansion
claim: Hyosung is investing about US$300m in a three-phase expansion of its ultra-high-voltage transformer plant in Memphis, Tennessee, and formed a JV with Quanta Services in June 2026 for extra-high-voltage circuit breakers; completion dates not given

name: LS Electric US manufacturing expansion (Texas, Utah)
claim: LS Electric plans US$240m of US investment by 2030, expanding its Utah switchgear plant and developing a Bastrop, Texas campus; transformer output at the Texas site is not confirmed

name: Minerals Security Partnership and successor FORGE
claim: Korea chaired the Minerals Security Partnership until June 2026; a February 2026 report says its 17 members carried into the successor FORGE; Korean public lenders joined the MSP Finance Network; no signed US-Korea critical-minerals MOU was found

name: Korea-Australia Free Trade Agreement (KAFTA)
claim: Signed in Seoul 8 Apr 2014 and in force 12 Dec 2014; Australia reached duty-free on all Korean imports from 1 Jan 2021 and Korean tariffs on Australian goods were phased out by 2023; RCEP is an alternative route.

name: RCEP (both members; in force for Korea 1 Feb 2022)
claim: DFAT notes RCEP entered into force for Korea on 1 Feb 2022 and may be used by exporters as an alternative to KAFTA; the member list shown here is partial.

name: Australia-Korea Comprehensive Strategic Partnership (2021)
claim: The 2021 partnership commits both to critical-mineral supply-chain resilience and a ministers' MoU, with a Critical Minerals Working Group on supply-chain mapping, R&D and investment; exact day not confirmed in the source.

name: Australia-Korea Critical Minerals Supply Chain partnership: A$50m initial Australian commitment
institution: Department of Industry, Science and Resources / Korea MOTIR
claim: Australia announced an initial A$50m for the critical-minerals partnership, with Korea to match subject to domestic processes; date and delivery not confirmed (sources place the MoU in 2021-22); USD value approximate.

name: Export Finance Australia-KEXIM MOU on critical-minerals co-financing
claim: EFA and the Export-Import Bank of Korea signed an MoU in Sep 2023 on co-financing in critical minerals and related sectors; no amounts given, and the day is approximate.

name: KOTRA-Austrade MOU revision (critical minerals, hydrogen, third markets)
claim: Revised 1988 MOU signed 30 Oct 2025 at APEC Gyeongju names critical minerals and hydrogen, joint third-market entry and resumed biennial consultations in Australia from 2026.

name: Albanese-Lee meeting, APEC Gyeongju
institution: Prime Minister of Australia / Korea Presidential Office
claim: Lee noted large Korean investment in Australian lithium, critical-minerals and rare-earth projects; no joint statement or deliverable found.

name: Albanese-Lee meeting at UN General Assembly, New York
institution: Prime Minister of Australia / Korea Presidential Office
claim: Albanese called Korea a trusted partner in critical minerals and clean energy at a Sep 2026 UNGA meeting, the third bilateral after the G7 and APEC; no deliverable reported; day approximate.

name: Australia-Korea Foreign and Defence 2+2 (sixth meeting, Melbourne)
institution: DFAT / Department of Defence / Korea MOFA-MND
claim: Sixth 2+2 met 1 May 2024 with a joint statement; no 2025-26 meeting was found, and the biennial cadence implies the next falls around 2026.

name: Minerals Security Partnership (Korea chair 2025)
claim: ASPI lists the MSP, which Korea chairs in 2025, among the frameworks for Australia-Korea minerals cooperation; Australian membership is not stated in that article.

name: POSCO Pilbara Lithium Solution hydroxide plant, Gwangyang (POSCO 82% / Pilbara Minerals 18%)
source: Mining Technology; Australian Mining Review (via search summary)
claim: Plant converts Pilgangoora spodumene to battery-grade hydroxide (43,000 t/yr nameplate); train 1 ramped in 2024 and train 2 was completed in early 2025; no 2026 production data found; day approximate.

name: US$460m non-recourse loan from two Korean state banks for POSCO-Pilbara hydroxide plant
claim: Two Korean government-owned banks funded US$460m for the Gwangyang plant, non-recourse to Pilbara Minerals; lender names and date not confirmed in the source seen; date approximate.

name: SK On three-year supply of up to 15,000 t lithium hydroxide from POSCO Pilbara JV
institution: SK On / POSCO Pilbara Lithium Solution
claim: Nov 2024 agreement lets SK On take up to 15,000 t of Korea-made hydroxide from Australian-sourced spodumene; POSCO Future M is to take 20,000 t a year; day approximate.

name: POSCO acquires stake in a Mineral Resources lithium mine
claim: POSCO's 4 Sep 2026 release says it acquired a stake in a high-quality lithium mine owned by Mineral Resources in 2026; mine name, stake size and amount are not given.

name: POSCO Holdings: Australia supplies about 70% of group raw materials
claim: At the 2 Sep 2026 AKBC-KABC meeting in Adelaide POSCO's chair said Australia supplies about 70% of the group's raw materials, as it has since 1971; POSCO also owns Senex Energy (2022); no new agreements were signed.

name: Korea Zinc: Sun Metals (Townsville) and Ark Energy SunHQ hydrogen hub
institution: Korea Zinc / Ark Energy / Sun Metals
claim: Korea Zinc has run Sun Metals since 1996; Ark Energy's SunHQ hub (1 MW electrolyser, solar-powered) drew a CEFC commitment of up to A$12.5m; an export feasibility study for hydrogen to Korea was reported; no 2025-26 status found.

name: Korea Zinc chair meets Albanese; Project Crucible and Australian smelting
institution: Korea Zinc / Prime Minister of Australia
claim: On 24 Jun 2026 Korea Zinc's chair met Albanese in Canberra on supply chains and smelting competitiveness and agreed to explore cooperation; Project Crucible is the US$7.4bn Tennessee smelter, not an Australian investment.

name: Calls to expand Sun Metals into an integrated critical-minerals refinery (Korea-US-Australia link)
claim: Townsville leaders and the US consul general back a trilateral supply chain with an expanded Sun Metals refinery; Sun Metals is studying feasibility, with no amount or commitment announced.

name: LGES-Liontown spodumene offtake, Kathleen Valley
claim: Binding term sheet Jan 2022 and full offtake May 2022 for spodumene concentrate; reported buyer termination right if production had not begun by 1 Sep 2025; current status not checked.

name: LGES-WesCEF (Wesfarmers) lithium concentrate offtake, Mt Holland, up to 85,000 t
institution: LG Energy Solution / Wesfarmers Chemicals, Energy and Fertilisers
source: ASPI Strategist; The Star (via search summary)
claim: Feb 2024 second agreement for up to 85,000 t of concentrate from Mt Holland, after a 2022 deal for 50,000 t of hydroxide; no value disclosed.

name: SK On-Lake Resources lithium offtake and 10% equity stake
claim: Oct 2022 five-year offtake (option for five more) with SK On taking a 10% stake in the ASX-listed Lake Resources; delivery status not confirmed in the source.

name: Hyundai-Kia NdPr offtake from Arafura Nolans; KEXIM LOI up to US$150m
institution: Hyundai Motor / Kia / Arafura Rare Earths / KEXIM
claim: Seven-year NdPr oxide offtake (600 t/yr rising to 1,500 t/yr) with conditions to be met by end-Jun 2026; KEXIM issued a letter of intent for up to US$150m debt; whether conditions were met or Nolans reached financing is not confirmed.

name: Australian Strategic Materials Korean Metals Plant, Ochang (neodymium metal and alloys)
claim: ASM's Korean plant opened in 2022 and produces neodymium metals and alloys (designed 5,200 t/yr); its Dubbo (NSW) mine, intended to feed it, has unclear funding in the sources seen.

name: ASM first commercial heavy rare earth sale from Cheongju plant (Jul 2025)
claim: ASM made its first commercial sale of terbium and dysprosium from its Korean plant in Jul 2025, to a Neo Performance Materials subsidiary; the buyer is not a Korean firm per the source; day approximate.

name: Australia Critical Minerals Strategic Reserve lists Korea as international partner
claim: The reserve (offtake-rights model) says it will support collaboration with partners including Korea; no Korean firm or Korea-specific offtake was found, and reports of share sales to allies are unconfirmed; date not recorded.

name: Marinus Link cable supply went to Prysmian, not a Korean maker
source: Baird Maritime; Offshore Engineer (via search summary)
claim: Prysmian holds the roughly EUR600m Marinus Link subsea cable contract, so LS Cable and Taihan are not supplying that project; date approximate.

name: Coverage gap: no Korea-Australia deals found for wind towers, NGO steel or Korean cable supply
source: Asiae (CS Wind contract disclosures; search negative)
claim: Searches found no CS Wind tower contract for an Australian wind farm (its sales run through Vietnam to Vestas, Siemens Gamesa and others) and no Korean cable or non-oriented electrical steel supply to Australian projects.

name: Canada-Korea Free Trade Agreement (CKFTA)
claim: Signed in Ottawa 22 Sep 2014 and in force 1 Jan 2015; Canada's first FTA in Asia-Pacific, covering goods, services, investment and procurement; nearly 90% of Canadian exports to Korea duty-free at entry into force.

name: Canada-Korea Comprehensive Strategic Partnership
source: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (news release 29 Jan 2026)
claim: The Comprehensive Strategic Partnership was launched in 2022 and is the base for the Jan 2026 industrial MOU; leaders agreed in Sep 2022 to develop a critical-minerals and energy MOU; day of launch inferred from the Sep 2022 summit.

name: Korea-Canada MOU on Critical Mineral Supply Chains, Clean Energy Transition and Energy Security
claim: Non-binding MOU (2023, not 2022) covering critical-mineral value chains, clean fuels and CCS, and clean-energy, ZEV and semiconductor manufacturing, with an action plan and investment-screening cooperation; it lets Korea count Canada toward the US EV-credit minerals test; exact signing date not confirmed.

name: Canada-Korea economic security 2+2 dialogue (first meeting 2023)
institution: Global Affairs Canada / ISED / Korea MOFA-MOTIE
claim: Economic-security 2+2 (Joly, Champagne, Park Jin, Ahn Dukgeun) launched Sep 2022 and first met in Seoul on 16 May 2023; priorities were critical minerals, clean energy, supply chains, AI and economic coercion; page itself not opened.

name: Canada-Korea Foreign and Defence 2+2, second meeting (Ottawa)
claim: Second 2+2 (first was Nov 2024) agreed to pursue an update of the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership Action Plan, start Defence Cooperation Agreement steps and coordinate on economic security; the statement does not mention critical minerals or energy; next meeting in Korea in 2028.

name: Canada-Korea Security and Defence Cooperation Partnership
claim: Carney and Lee welcomed the partnership at the Gyeongju APEC summit on 30 Oct 2025, Canada's first in the Indo-Pacific, and finalised a classified-information agreement that supports defence procurement; the readout does not mention energy, critical minerals or LNG.

name: MOU on Canada-Korea industrial collaboration in future mobility; Canada-Korea Industrial Cooperation Committee
institution: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada / Korea MOTIR
source: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (news release)
claim: Joly and Korea's Trade, Industry and Resources Minister Kim Jung-kwan signed in Ottawa; sets up an industrial cooperation committee and a forum on a Korean auto footprint, battery production, materials processing and critical-minerals recycling; no amounts or companies named.

name: Hodgson-Kang meeting: joint critical-minerals stockpiling plan
claim: On 2 Jun 2026 Canada and Korea agreed to develop a joint critical-minerals stockpiling plan by end-2026, discussed strategic-resource investments, and Korea agreed to facilitate CKFTA preferential tariffs for Canadian crude; no volumes or amounts given.

name: GSC-KIGAM implementation agreement on natural hydrogen R&D
institution: Natural Resources Canada (Geological Survey of Canada) / KIGAM
claim: The Geological Survey of Canada and Korea's KIGAM signed an implementation agreement on naturally occurring hydrogen research and development, announced with the 2 Jun 2026 energy and critical-minerals meeting.

name: KOGAS stake in LNG Canada (Phase I investor; Phase II prospective partner)
claim: KOGAS is a key investor in LNG Canada Phase I and a prospective partner in Phase II, whose final investment decision is expected later in 2026; Korea plans to import at least 1.4 Mt a year of Canadian LNG for 30+ years once Phase II is at full output.

name: Canada-Korea trade 2025: energy and ores lead Canadian exports
claim: In 2025 energy products were Canada's largest export to Korea (C$2.2bn) and metal ores and non-metallic minerals second (C$1.5bn); the release names no uranium, nuclear or SMR cooperation.

name: Canada policy on foreign state-owned investment in critical minerals (Investment Canada Act)
institution: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
claim: Policy of Oct 2022: acquisitions of control of Canadian critical-minerals businesses by foreign state-owned or state-influenced enterprises approved only on an exceptional basis; it is not Korea-specific and no source found applying it to Korean firms.

name: Canada steel tariff-rate quotas and surtax; Korean complaint
institution: Department of Finance Canada / Korea MOTIR
claim: From 26 Dec 2025 Canada cut FTA-partner steel quotas to 75% of 2024 volumes with a 50% over-quota surtax; Korea protested that this breaches the CKFTA and sought an exemption, none found; whether non-oriented electrical steel is covered is not confirmed.

name: Canada submarine programme: TKMS selected over Hanwha Ocean (KSS-III)
source: Korea JoongAng Daily; Asia Pacific Foundation of Canada
claim: Carney named Germany's TKMS preferred supplier for up to 12 submarines on 6 Jul 2026 (NATO interoperability cited); contracting runs through 2027 and Canada kept the option to open talks with Hanwha Ocean if TKMS talks fail.

name: Hanwha Ocean industrial-benefit offers tied to Canadian steel and technology
claim: Hanwha's bid carried MOUs on steel, satellite communications, AI, space and sensors plus Canadian steel use and technology transfer; the article does not link the bid to energy, critical minerals or batteries; offers lapse unless Canada reopens talks.

name: Carney-Lee meeting at G7 (Evian) on defence, energy and critical minerals
institution: Prime Minister's Office Canada / Korea Presidential Office
claim: Lee and Carney agreed on 16 Jun 2026 to strengthen cooperation in defence, security, energy and critical minerals; an informal meeting followed at the NATO summit; no deliverables or amounts reported.

name: POSCO Future M-GM Ultium CAM cathode plant, Becancour (Quebec)
claim: JV owned 85% by POSCO Future M and 15% by GM; phase 1 (20,000 t/yr high-nickel cathode, all for Ultium Cells) was scheduled for late Oct 2026 after earlier delays; phase 2 timing unconfirmed; no source found confirming start-up has occurred.

name: EcoPro BM-SK On-Ford cathode plant, Becancour (Quebec)
source: S&P Global Mobility; Korean press (via search summary)
claim: C$1.2bn, 45,000 t/yr plant (originally 1H 2026) was halted twice in 2024 and resumed in Sep 2024; one undated Korean report says Ford is leaving; current status and ownership not confirmed in any 2026 source; USD figure is the 2023 announcement value.

name: NextStar Energy cell plant, Windsor (LGES-Stellantis)
claim: Series cell production began Nov 2025 and the plant was officially opened in Mar 2026, initially focused on stationary storage; employment 1,300+ against a 2,500 target.

name: LG Energy Solution buys Stellantis 49% stake in NextStar Energy
claim: LGES agreed in early Feb 2026 to take full ownership of NextStar by buying Stellantis's 49%, with Stellantis staying a customer; closing subject to approvals and not confirmed; publication day approximate.

name: LGES supply MOUs with Electra, Avalon and Snow Lake (cobalt sulphate, lithium hydroxide)
claim: In 2022 LGES signed non-binding MOUs for 7,000 t of cobalt sulphate over three years from 2023 and 55,000 t of lithium hydroxide over five years from 2025; signing date inferred from the Sep 2022 Toronto visit; later delivery not confirmed.

name: Hydro Lithium 10-year offtake of Prairie Lithium Phase 1 output (Saskatchewan brine)
source: Prairie Lithium ASX announcement (via search summary)
claim: Binding agreement for 100% of Phase 1 (about 150 t/yr LCE) for ten years, renewable to 30; crystallite reported to be refined in Korea, first production targeted Q4 2026; sources differ on whether Hydro Lithium is Korean-based.

name: Samsung SDI US$18.5m investment in Canada Nickel (Crawford project option)
claim: Samsung SDI bought 15.6m Canada Nickel shares for US$18.5m with an option on 10% of the Crawford nickel-cobalt sulphide project carrying offtake rights; date not shown in the source.

name: KHNP-ARC-NB Power ARC-100 SMR at Point Lepreau (New Brunswick)
institution: Korea Hydro & Nuclear Power / ARC Clean Technology / NB Power
source: Korea Times; NEI Magazine (via search summary)
claim: Non-binding KHNP, ARC and NB Power agreements (MOU Nov 2023, trilateral May 2024, Dec 2024 partnership) for the ARC-100 SMR targeting commissioning around 2030; no 2025-26 update found; publication day approximate.

name: Reported 10-year Cameco uranium supply deal with KHNP
claim: One trade report describes a 10-year Cameco supply deal with KHNP but gives no date, and no Cameco or KHNP release was found; KHNP's confirmed 2025 enrichment deal is with US-based Centrus.

name: Cameco backs Westinghouse settlement with KEPCO and KHNP
claim: Cameco publicly supported the Jan 2025 resolution of Westinghouse's IP dispute with KEPCO and KHNP, calling it a framework for further reactor deployments; a link to Canadian uranium or conversion supply is not stated.

name: Coverage gap: no Korea-Canada deals found for NGO steel, power cables or aluminium wire rod
claim: Searches found no Korean-Canadian investment, offtake or supply deal in non-oriented electrical steel, power cables or aluminium wire rod; the Jan 2026 MOU names only automotive, batteries, critical minerals and AI.
